note: Reel 12: Cyclone Arnab. Arnab crossed the coast near Narsapur on 28 Oct 2026, a year to the day after Montha; the Bay of Bengal's late-October season, the steering, the surge (1977), and the root cause of the difference: warnings and shelters. Kokoro af_heart, speed 1.0. Plain spellings throughout: the phoneme /ˈɑɹnəb/ came out as "Arnub", the plain Arnab right (first run). Numbers are written as spoken, so the display words match the voice's word tokens one to one. 148 words. Facts: docs/research.md.

lines.text: Cyclone Arnab hit Andhra Pradesh near Narsapur, on the twenty-eighth of October.
A year earlier, to the day, Cyclone Montha hit the same coast.
That's not a coincidence. It's a season.
All summer, monsoon winds tear storms apart. In October they drop, over a sea that's still warm.
And at this time of year, the Bay's storms are steered north-west. Straight at this coast.
The Bay of Bengal makes one in twenty of the world's cyclones, but historically, most of the deaths.
Its shallow, funnel-shaped sea piles up surges. In nineteen seventy-seven, a six-metre surge on this coast killed at least ten thousand people.
Arnab was a very severe cyclone. But this time, over fifty thousand people were moved before it hit.
The root cause of the difference? Not weaker storms. Warnings days ahead, and shelters built after that storm.
Next October, the Bay will be warm again.

ref_text: The night was cold and very quiet.
